title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down and struck through with a single diagonal line. Read the right way up, it is a sketch of an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms on simplices, with values in a 'coefficient datum' (A,Π,γ).

(1) Linear data of the simplex. For a finite index set I there is the exact sequence 0→Z→Z×Z^I, with the map given by (−id, diag). Its cokernel is a lattice of rank |I| (isomorphic to Z^I), which plays the role of the 'inhomogeneous linear functions' on the affine simplex. The homogeneous version is Z^I/Z. The candidate algebra of forms is
- Γ_*((Z×Z^I)/Z) ⊗_Z Λ^*_Z(Z^I/Z), or
- Γ_*(Z^I/Z) ⊗ Λ^*(Z^I/Z).
These are contrasted with the naive Sym_*(Z^(I)) ⊗ Λ^* Z^(I), whose divided-power version is preferred.

(2) Concretely, the forms on the simplex Δ^I with coefficients in (A,Π,γ) are
Ω_I = A{(X_i),dX_i} / (ΣX_i − Π, ΣdX_i).
Here:
- A{…} is the divided-power polynomial algebra.
- dX_i are odd generators.
- The barycentric relation ΣX_i = 1 of Sullivan forms is replaced by ΣX_i = Π, with Π a chosen element of A.

(3) Functoriality in the coefficients. A morphism (A,Π,γ)→(A',Π',γ') is a pair (φ,λ) with φ(Π) = λΠ' and φ(Π^{[x]}) = λ^x Π'^{[x]}. The coordinates are rescaled by X_i ↦ λX_i, giving Ω_I(A) → A'{X_i,dX_i}/(ΣX_i − Π', ΣdX_i). The note 'définir de façon cohérente … en (A,Π,γ)' and the symbol C^*(X,(A,Π,γ)) indicate the goal: a cochain functor on simplicial sets X, natural in this coefficient datum. It would be given by an end/limit of Ω_{Δ^n} over the simplices of X.

(4) At the top of the page (written first) he records the axioms of the target structure (A^*,d,γ):
- graded anticommutative: xy = (−1)^{deg x deg y} yx, and x^2 = 0 for x of odd degree;
- d^2 = 0, with Leibniz rule d(xy) = (dx)y + (−1)^{deg x} x dy;
- divided powers γ_n with deg γ_n = n·deg, x^{[n]} 'like' x^n/n!.
He also does sample computations of the divided square of a sum of 3-forms and of products of sums.

What it serves: building an integral (Z- or PD-ring-coefficient) commutative-type de Rham/Sullivan cochain model with divided powers. This is presumably for the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the PD de Rham complex. Over Z the PD Poincaré lemma holds because d(x^{[n+1]}) = x^{[n]}dx, so such simplicial forms have a chance to compute integral cohomology.

The auxiliary element Π, with its λ^x scaling, looks like a normalisation constant ('period', à la 2πi / Tate twist). It makes the construction equivariant under rescaling.

The neighbouring pages are about something else: truncation and adjoint functors on graded module categories.
errors: The formula (Σ y_{ijk} dX_i dX_j dX_k)^{[2]} = Σ_{i,j,k,i',j',k'} y_{ijk} y_{i'j'k'} … is problematic. A 3-form has odd degree, so it carries no divided powers (and its square is 0). Even for even degree, a divided square must be a sum over unordered pairs plus γ_2 of the individual terms, not a sum over all ordered pairs, which gives x^2 rather than x^{[2]}. It reads as a scratch computation, not a claim.
The rescaling rule φ(Π(x)) = λ^x Π'(x) is only sensible if Π(x) means Π^{[x]} (divided powers of Π). This is consistent with γ but not stated.

ideas.what: Simplicial polynomial differential forms with divided powers: A{X_i,dX_i}/(ΣX_i−Π, ΣdX_i), assembled into cochains C^*(X,(A,Π,γ)) of a simplicial set X
ideas.modern_name: Integral / PD analogue of Sullivan's A_PL polynomial forms (divided-power simplicial de Rham forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977, rational case); H. Cartan 1976 'Théories cohomologiques'; integral 'tame'/divided-power forms are associated with Cenkl–Porter (late 1970s–80s)

ideas.what: Replacing the barycentric normalisation ΣX_i=1 by ΣX_i=Π, with functoriality (φ,λ), φ(Π)=λΠ', φ(Π^{[x]})=λ^xΠ'^{[x]}
ideas.modern_name: Twisted/normalised simplicial forms; a 'period' or Tate-twist-like normalisation of the coefficient ring

ideas.what: Description of forms on Δ^I via Γ_*((Z×Z^I)/Z) ⊗ Λ^*(Z^I/Z) using the sequence 0→Z→Z×Z^I
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power algebra on affine linear functions of the simplex (PD symmetric algebra of the affine dual)

ideas.what: Axioms of a graded anticommutative DG algebra with divided powers (deg γ_n = n·deg, x^2=0 in odd degree)

missed.claim: Around 1975–76 Grothendieck sketched an integral (divided-power) version of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms. The coefficients are a ring A with an element Π, normalising the barycentric coordinates by ΣX_i = Π, and with rescaling functoriality (φ,λ). The aim was a cochain functor C^*(X,(A,Π,γ)) on simplicial sets. This predates or parallels Cenkl–Porter's integral 'tame' forms, and the Π-normalisation does not seem to appear in the later literature.
missed.quote: A{(X_i),dX_i}/{ΣX_i − Π, ΣdX_i} ... C^*(X,(A,Π,γ)) ... définir de façon cohérente ... en (A,Π,γ) ... φ(Π)=λΠ', φ(Π(x))=λ^xΠ'(x)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral commutative-type cochain models (PD cdgas, E∞ cochains, Mandell's theorem, Yuan's integral models, Toën's affine stacks) are an active topic. A version twisted by a period-like Π with λ^x scaling suggests a weight/Tate-twist structure on simplicial PD forms, possibly related to comparison isomorphisms. It is worth checking whether the lecture notes develop it further.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a struck-out draft, but it documents that Grothendieck in 1975–76 was setting up integral divided-power simplicial de Rham forms with an unusual Π-normalised coefficient datum. That is close to, and roughly contemporaneous with, Sullivan and Cartan, and anticipates integral 'tame' forms. The Π/λ^x device is unusual. Little is finished, though, and the PD Poincaré-lemma idea itself is standard.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down. The first expression should read Γ_*((Z×Z^I)/Z) ⊗_Z Λ^*_Z(Z^I/Z), i.e. Z×Z^I over Z, not Z/(Z×Z^I).
'Π(x)' in φ(Π(x)) = λ^x Π'(x) is likely Π^{[x]} or a shorthand for divided powers of Π.
The superscript in '(Σ y_{ijk} dX_i dX_j dX_k)^{[ ]}' is likely [2] (divided square).
The top block is the list of DG-PD algebra axioms for (A^*,d,γ): 'alg. graduée anticommutative … puissances divisées … (x^2=0 si deg x impair)', with deg γ_n(x) = n·deg x.
